S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.

subtypes.With Depressed Mood: Symptoms mainly include low mood, tearfulness, or feelings of hopelessness.
subtypes.With Anxiety: Symptoms mainly include nervousness, worry, jitteriness, or separation anxiety.
subtypes.With Mixed Anxiety and Depressed Mood: A combination of depression and anxiety symptoms appears.
subtypes.With Disturbance of Conduct: Symptoms mainly involve violation of rules, truancy, vandalism, reckless driving, or fighting.
subtypes.With Mixed Disturbance of Emotions and C: Both emotional symptoms (depression, anxiety) and behavioral problems appear together.
subtypes.Unspecified: Maladaptive reactions not classified into the above types (e.g., physical complaints, social withdrawal).

patient_info.stressor: Ariel’s plant brought in a new operations manager who questioned her long-standing quality-control methods and abruptly rewrote several procedures she had helped build. At first she treated the conflict like a process problem to solve, but over the next two months her reaction to every meeting with him began spilling into her evenings, her marriage, and the careful routines that usually kept her grounded. Her work became impaired when she started missing internal deadlines, avoiding cross-functional meetings, and second-guessing inspection decisions she had previously handled confidently. After a tense performance discussion with HR, she accepted an Employee Assistance Program referral and was scheduled for a psychiatric evaluation.

S081.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
S081.description: Emotional or behavioral symptoms appearing in response to an identifiable stressor.
S081.manifestation: I’m here because ever since this new operations manager started picking apart the inspection procedures I’ve used for years, I can’t seem to leave work at work—I come home wound up, snap at my husband, lie awake replaying meetings, and then the next day I second-guess routine quality calls I used to make without trouble.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Symptoms must develop within 3 months of the onset of the stressor
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I was doing fine before the new operations manager came in, and the trouble started building within weeks of his changes to our procedures. By the second month, I knew my reactions to him were affecting me well beyond the workday.

additional_requirement_2.name: Additional Requirement 2
additional_requirement_2.description: Within 6 months of the termination of the stressor or its consequences
additional_requirement_2.manifestation: This situation hasn’t really ended yet—I still have to report to him and deal with the procedures he changed. I haven’t had any period after it was resolved where these problems kept going for months on their own.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My work record has taken a hit because I’ve missed internal deadlines and pulled back from meetings I’m expected to attend. At home, my husband and I are arguing more, and I’m not keeping up with our usual evening routines the way I used to.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about two months, since the new operations manager started changing my inspection procedures.
